title: Replace a staged renderer attribute deliberately
goal: Replace a known pending attribute after constructing an owned render tree when building an advanced renderer integration. Use the experimental indexed operation before submission; ordinary components should render their final values directly.

selectionNotes: Replace a known pending attribute after constructing an owned render tree when building an advanced renderer integration. Use the experimental indexed operation before submission; ordinary components should render their final values directly.

renderingModes: Advanced in-process custom Renderer and HtmlRenderer output only; no browser DOM adapter, live batch mutation or stable rendering abstraction.
prerequisites: Use all files below as one project per release, including wwwroot when present. The .NET 10 comparison remains valid; no new API route on net10.0 is claimed.
constraints: Moss Gallery stages a figure caption, then selects its final value before BuildRenderTree returns. The .NET 10 path rebuilds this tiny owned tree; this remains valid on .NET 11.

The argument is a zero-based frame index, not a source sequence number. Index 1 is established by this fixed tree; production adapters must track their own attribute frame and reject other layouts. Duplicate-attribute processing can move frames.
Only replace a staged attribute of the same intended meaning. This sample has a plain string data attribute; changing event callbacks/handler IDs or parameter contracts is outside scope.

Setting null leaves an attribute frame with a null value. It does not replay AddAttribute omission rules or compact the tree. The real HTML renderer omits this null-valued attribute; that output does not imply the frame disappeared.

Wrong frame type throws InvalidOperationException. Negative or count-or-higher indices throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Do not edit GetFrames().Array, retained renderer frames or an already submitted RenderBatch.
optIns: Local #pragma warning disable/restore ASP0032 around SetAttributeValue, with BL0006 confined to intentional frame/Renderer boundaries. Never suppress these project-wide.
stabilityLimitations: Experimental API; compatibility can change. Actual evidence: SDK 10.0.402 / runtime 10.0.13 and SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105 / runtime 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105. GA reconciliation and comprehensive publication remain open.

evidence.scope: Both real consumers compile and execute through Record-Evidence.ps1. Four custom-renderer batches and four actual HTML outputs cover replacement, encoding, null and subsequent replacement. The RC2 consumer executes wrong-frame and both index-boundary failures; Test-StagedAttribute.ps1 compiles independent negative consumers for CS1061, ASP0032 and BL0006. No DOM, event-handler mutation, performance or cross-version renderer compatibility is claimed.
